newsitem.title: FRANCE: Clarins sees double-digit 1996 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Clarins sees double-digit 1996 profit rise.

text.p: Skincare and cosmetics firm Clarins said on Tuesday that it expected to show double-digit profit growth for 1996 when it reports its results on April 21.
"Based on initial indications, the 1996 results should show double-digit growth," Clarins said in a statement reporting a 15.8 percent rise in 1996 turnover to 2.97 billion francs.

It said "1996 was characterised by sustained levels of activity, successful launches in all sectors, the creation of two new distribution subsidiaries and the successful integration of the Parfac group, which owns the Azzaro and Montana perfumes."
Excluding Parfac, consolidated from July 1995, Clarins' 1996 sales showed a rise of 9.1 percent.
It said the perfume business had exceeded its sales target of 800 million francs and now represents 27.3 percent of consolidated sales.
"Parfac's contribution, after financial expenses and goodwill amortisation, will be positive," Clarins said.
The family-run firm began to expand from its core skincare business in 1991.
